before.title: Fuel Gauge Sending Unit Failure
before.description: Some M35 owners report inaccurate fuel level readings, including gauges that stick, read empty when fuel remains, or fluctuate unexpectedly. The issue is commonly related to wear or contamination in the fuel level sending unit inside the tank, which can affect trip planning and trigger low-fuel warnings incorrectly.
before.solution: Compare gauge behavior to actual fill volume and scan for fuel level sensor data if available. Repair typically requires replacement of the faulty fuel level sending unit or pump module assembly, depending on which side of the saddle tank is affected. Because tank access is labor-intensive, many owners replace related seals and inspect the pump assembly at the same time.
symptoms: Fuel gauge reads empty with fuel in tank
Low fuel warning comes on too early

citations.title: NHTSA complaints involving inaccurate fuel gauge readings on Infiniti M35

communityRecommendations.content: Denso fuel pump-related components are often preferred because owners report better reliability than no-name assemblies.
Track mileage manually until the repair is completed, since the gauge may not be trustworthy.
If the tank is being opened, replace the seal and inspect wiring connectors to prevent future access-related leaks or faults.

before.title: Radiator Cracking and Coolant Leaks
before.description: Aging M35 radiators can develop cracks at the plastic end tanks or seams, leading to coolant loss and overheating risk. The issue is usually age-related thermal cycling rather than a single defect, and it becomes more common on higher-mileage cars.
before.solution: Pressure-test the cooling system and inspect the radiator end tanks, hose necks, and seams for seepage or dried coolant residue. Repair generally means replacing the radiator, refreshing upper and lower hoses if brittle, and refilling with the correct coolant while bleeding air from the system. If overheating occurred, the thermostat should also be checked or replaced as preventive maintenance.

citations.title: NHTSA complaints mentioning radiator leaks and overheating on Infiniti M35

communityRecommendations.content: Denso radiators are often recommended as a reliable replacement with fitment close to OEM.
Replace the radiator cap and inspect hoses during the same job to avoid chasing another cooling leak later.
Do not continue driving if the temperature gauge rises, because the VQ engine can suffer expensive overheating damage.

before.title: Brake Rotor Warping and Front Brake Vibration
before.description: Infiniti service bulletin ITB00-024I applies to all Infiniti vehicles and defines brake judder as vibration felt through the vehicle, steering wheel or brake pedal while braking. The bulletin identifies rotor thickness variation and/or rotor runout as the cause; brake-pedal pulsation and, in severe cases, steering-wheel oscillation can result.
before.solution: Verify the condition with the driver and a road test. Infiniti directs technicians to correct brake judder by machining the rotors with an approved on-car brake lathe. If a rotor is replaced, index it to the axle hub for minimum runout, tighten lug nuts evenly with a torque wrench, and burnish serviced brakes as specified in ITB00-024I.

before.title: Camshaft and Crankshaft Position Sensor Failure
before.description: The VQ35DE engine used in the M35 is known for intermittent camshaft and crankshaft position sensor failures. Heat and age can cause the sensors to send erratic signals, leading to hard starting, stalling, limp mode, or a check engine light.
before.solution: Scan for stored fault codes and monitor cam/crank synchronization data while checking harness condition near the sensors. Repair typically involves replacing the failed camshaft position sensor(s) and sometimes the crankshaft position sensor with quality parts, then clearing codes and confirming proper restart behavior. Using OEM-supplier sensors is strongly preferred because cheap sensors often cause repeat failures.

citations.title: NHTSA complaints for Infiniti M35 involving camshaft/crankshaft sensor stalling

communityRecommendations.content: Denso sensors are commonly recommended because they match OEM performance better than low-cost generic replacements.
If one cam sensor fails, many owners replace both cam sensors and the crank sensor together to avoid repeat breakdowns.
Clear codes only after confirming battery voltage is healthy, since weak voltage can complicate diagnosis.

before.title: Dashboard Melting and Cracking
before.description: Owners of 2006-2010 Infiniti M35 models frequently report the upper dashboard becoming sticky, shiny, cracked, or melting when exposed to heat and sunlight. The problem is tied to deterioration of the dash pad material, which can create glare on the windshield and worsen over time in hot climates.
before.solution: Diagnosis is visual: inspect the dash surface for tackiness, warping, cracks, and reflected glare. Repair usually requires replacement of the dashboard pad or full upper dash assembly, as cleaning products do not permanently fix the material breakdown. Used parts may reduce cost, but many owners prefer a new OEM-style replacement due to fit and appearance concerns; labor is substantial because the dash must be removed.
symptoms: Cracks forming near vents or instrument panel
Shiny melted appearance in hot weather

citations.title: NHTSA complaints discussing cracked and melting dashboard on Infiniti M35

communityRecommendations.content: Use a windshield sunshade and park out of direct sun to slow further deterioration.
Owners often use an aftermarket dash cover as a temporary fix to reduce glare and hide cracks when full replacement is too expensive.
Avoid silicone-heavy dressings because they can increase glare and may worsen the sticky feel.

before.title: Front Lower Control Arm and Bushing Wear
before.description: The M35 commonly develops wear in the front lower control arms, tension rod bushings, and related suspension joints, especially as mileage climbs. This causes looseness in the front suspension, uneven tire wear, and clunking over bumps or during braking.
before.solution: Inspect the front suspension for torn bushings, leaking hydraulic bushings, and play in the ball joints or control arms. Repair usually involves replacing the affected lower control arms and/or tension rods, followed by a four-wheel alignment. Aftermarket complete arm assemblies are popular because they save labor compared with pressing bushings separately.
symptoms: Clunking or knocking from front suspension

citations.title: NHTSA complaints referencing front suspension noise and control arm wear

communityRecommendations.content: Moog complete control arms are commonly recommended because they simplify installation and are widely available.
Replace worn tension rods at the same time if braking shimmy is present, then get an alignment immediately.
Inspect inner tire wear before buying tires, since suspension bushing wear often causes rapid edge wear.
